train.info.title: The practice modes
train.info.intro: Six ways through the same repertoire. They differ in WHAT they ask you and how much of a line you play.
train.info.timed: Single positions against the clock for three minutes, against one personal best. It draws on everything you have saved, including paused and shallow lines, so it stays playable early on.
train.info.missed: One move at a time, from the positions you have actually got wrong. No run-up: you are dropped straight into the position that beat you.
train.info.doorDetail: One pass through your whole book, asking every move exactly once. Lines that share an opening replay it once here instead of once per line, which is why it is much shorter than drilling the same lines one by one.

train.info.saving.one: one move you’d otherwise answer twice
train.info.saving.other: {n} repeated moves you’d otherwise answer twice

train.info.new: Full runs of your newest lines, start to finish. The one to use straight after building something, while it is still fresh enough to fix.
train.info.weak: Full runs of the lines you score worst on. Same shape as the one above, picked from the other end of the list.
train.info.prep: Full runs of the lines you tagged against a scouted opponent. It only appears once you have some.
train.info.footnote: Time attack and Review missed moves ask single positions; the rest walk whole lines. Nothing here changes your review schedule differently — a move answered is a move reviewed, whichever door you came in by.

settings.resetSyncs: You’re signed in, so the reset syncs to your account and your other devices.
settings.leaveMeOutOf: Leave me out of the counts
settings.theAppCountsAnonymous: The app counts anonymous events like “a line was saved” — no cookies, no identifier, nothing that says it was you. Turn this on and this device stops contributing to those counts. It covers anonymous usage counting only — if you’re signed in, see the privacy policy for what your account itself stores.
settings.elegantIsAFelt: Elegant is a felt-table green; Gamer is a neon-glow dark. System follows your phone’s light/dark setting.
settings.newSetsDownloadOnce: New sets download once, then stay cached.
settings.howMovesAreWritten: How moves are written everywhere: plain letters (Nf3, Bxf7) or piece symbols (♞f3, ♝xf7).
settings.theAHAnd: The a–h and 1–8 labels tucked into the board corners.
settings.aTinyBoardOn: A tiny board on every saved-line and suggestion card, showing where the line ends up.
settings.startTheEngineAutomatically: Start the engine automatically whenever you open the board. Either way, the engine button on the board turns it on or off at any time.
settings.aSoftToneOn: A soft tone on right and wrong moves while training.
settings.aRepertoireIsA: A repertoire is a book of lines of one colour. You start with two — White and Black — and for most people that is the whole story. More are for situations rather than colours: one for blitz, one for a tournament, one prepared for a particular opponent.
settings.doOneCleanRun: Do one clean run before a line joins training. Off adds it straight away.
settings.howManyNeverTrained: How many never-trained moves a session brings in each day. Reviews are never limited.
settings.wrongTriesAllowedBefore: Wrong tries allowed before the answer arrow shows.
settings.howFastThePlay: How fast the play button auto-plays a line.
settings.whatStartTrainingLaunches: What “Start training” launches from the Today screen.
settings.trainTabsAreBack: Train tabs are back in their first order
settings.longPressATab: Long-press a tab on Train and drag it to reorder. Train opens on the first one.
settings.pullYourRecentGames: Pull your recent games from Chess.com or Lichess to see which openings you actually play, where you score badly, and what to prep next.
settings.alsoPullGamesFrom: Also pull games from {site} into this same library.
settings.filtersTheLiveOpening: Filters the live opening statistics to games played at a rating band, so the numbers describe the opponents you actually get.
settings.noRatingFoundSet: No rating found — set one below, or import your games.
settings.everyRatedLichessGame: Every rated Lichess game, whatever the level.
settings.chosenForYouTap: chosen for you — tap a band to change it
settings.checksForNewGames: Checks for new games about once a week, when you open the app.
settings.readsYourImportedGames: Reads your imported games while the app is open — mistakes first, then the endgames you reached — so the Middlegame and Endgames boxes on Train fill in without you starting a scan.
settings.thisClearsEveryTraining: This clears every training score, streak and timed best, and marks all moves as never-trained. Your lines, notes and tags are kept. This can’t be undone.
settings.progressResetEveryLine: Progress reset ✓ — every line is due again.
settings.startTheSpacedRepetition: Start the spaced-repetition schedule over without deleting any lines.
settings.replaceThisDeviceFrom: Replace this device from your account
settings.yourDevicesNormallyMerge: Your devices normally merge, so nothing is ever lost. This does the other thing: it deletes what’s on this phone and restores exactly what your account holds. Use it after tidying up on another device.
settings.theLinesGamesStatistics: The lines, games, statistics and settings on this device are deleted and replaced with your account’s copy. Anything here that never reached the account is lost. Export a backup first if you’re not sure.
settings.closeYourBitoChess: Close your Bito Chess account and delete the copy of your data stored with it. This is permanent, it can’t be undone, and it doesn’t refund a purchase.
settings.alsoEraseEverythingOn: Also erase everything on this phone. Leave this off and your lines stay here, offline, exactly as they are.
settings.clearsWhatTheScan: Clears what the scan found in your games and starts the Middlegame exercises over. Your games and their analysis are kept.
settings.thisClearsEverySpot:
This clears every spot the scan has found and every one you have marked fixed, then reads your games from scratch. Every brilliant move you have re-found, every detective case you have cracked and every which-move question you have answered becomes available again too.

Your games and their saved analysis are untouched, so nothing you have written is lost — the same finds will be there again once the re-read is done.
settings.clearedYourGamesAre: Cleared — your games are being read again.
settings.clearedSwitchBackgroundAnalysis: Cleared. Switch background analysis on above to read them again.
settings.deleteAllYourData: Delete all your data and start over from scratch — lines, training history, imported games, opponents and preferences. There is no undo.
settings.thisPermanentlyDeletesEverythin: This permanently deletes everything Bito Chess keeps on this device: all your lines, every training score and your streak, imported games, scouted opponents, and all preferences. The app returns to a brand-new state.
settings.thereIsNoCloud: There is no cloud copy. If you might want any of it back, export a backup first.
settings.thisCannotBeUndone: This cannot be undone. The app will close and reopen empty, exactly as if you had just installed it.

builder.everyMovePlayedFrom:
Every move played from the position on the board, most popular first, with a bar saying how each has actually scored. Tap one to play it onto your line.

Masters is over-the-board games between titled players — established theory. Lichess is rated online games, filtered to a rating band, so the numbers describe the opponents you actually get.

A built-in set of common positions works offline with no login. Connecting Lichess extends it to every position, live — no personal data is read.
builder.todaySLineTo:
Today’s line to grow. You’ve been round this one enough times to know it, so the useful next step is depth rather than another run — the board is standing at the end of it, where your prep currently stops.

The moves listed are what your opponent could play from here, and why each one is worth an answer. Tap one, play your reply, and add it. One move is the whole job; every other tab is still here if you want to look further before you decide.
builder.threeMovesWorthHaving:
Three moves worth having here, picked from the games you’ve imported, the opening library and the engine. Tap one to play it onto your line.

Under them, each move’s record: how you’ve scored with it against how the database has. Turn on Auto-reply and the opponent’s answer is played for you, so you only ever choose your own moves.
builder.whatHappensFromThe:
What happens from the position on the board, from three sources: your own saved lines, your imported games, and any opponent you’ve scouted.

Tap a move to follow it. “Show tree” opens the whole thing as a map, and the bin on one of your own moves takes that continuation out of your book.
builder.everythingAboutTheLine:
Everything about the line you’re standing in: whether it’s in training, its tags, a note on the move on the board, and how often it should come round.

Below that, how the line has actually been going — how often it turns up in your games, how much of it you remember, and which move keeps breaking.
builder.theGameYouRe:
The game you’re looking at, move by move. “Analyse game” has the engine mark every move, and the marks then show in the move list and on the board.

Playing a different move here keeps the game intact and adds your move as a variation. “Save line” files the moves up to the board as a repertoire line; “Builder” takes them into the builder to carry on with.
builder.stockfishOnThePosition:
Stockfish on the position on the board: the evaluation bar, and the strongest continuations it can find. Opening this tab switches the engine on.

Tap one of its lines to play the move onto your own. An evaluation is an opinion about the position, not about whether the move belongs in your repertoire — that is what the other tabs are for.
